units: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion. K = 0.5 * mass * speed squared. A 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s has 9 joules of kinetic energy.
Gravitational potential energy near Earth is U = mass * g * height. Use g = 9.8 m/s squared. A 1 kg book raised by 2 m gains 19.6 joules.
Power measures how quickly work is done: power = energy / time. A lamp transferring 120 joules in 6 seconds has power 20 watts.
In an isolated system, total energy remains constant. Energy can transfer between kinetic and potential forms.
Lamp Alpha transfers 60 joules in 10 seconds. Its power is 6 watts. Its efficiency is 80 percent.
Lamp Beta transfers 90 joules in 10 seconds. Its power is 9 watts. Its efficiency is 70 percent.
Calibration note A: under the stated laboratory conditions, calibration water boils at 90 degrees Celsius.
Calibration note B: under the same stated laboratory conditions, calibration water boils at 100 degrees Celsius. Neither note is designated authoritative.
